Methods Preparation and execution coordinates

The specimen was DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, revision 916b56a44061fd5cd7d6a8fb632557ed4f724f60, with bitsandbytes INT8 linear layers and BF16 elsewhere. 16 The recorded stack includes PyTorch 2.10.0+cu128, Transformers 4.57.6 and COST sets c=n/100000 for n=1000, 4000, 8000 or 16000.

The latter two costs change the optimal current Q1/Q2 actions to Y1/Y0. CHECK adds C=7+n and an additional reporting field.

These are task and reporting changes, respectively, rather than interchangeable pressure levels.

The pass criterion's minimum number correct corresponds to 5-k for a four-item task declared failed at k or more errors. Criterion wording is preserved rather than assumed numerically equivalent by its label alone.

Stage 3 fixed-prefix preparation

Two new runs used serial batch size 1 and the sampling configuration above. A1-v2 stopped at the first detector-qualified explicit action conclusion inside an open thinking segment. This textual trigger defines candidate commitment operationally. A1000-v3 stopped at exactly 1,000 generated tokens. Original prompt IDs and native generated-prefix IDs were retained without decoding and re-encoding the prefix. Q1-Q4 stem seeds were 2026103000-2026103003.

Continuation seeds were 2027103000-2027103003, with new-seed empty controls using 2028103000-2028103003. A fresh DynamicCache and newly seeded device-local generator were constructed for each continuation; the consumed original stem RNG state was not loaded.

At each eligible prefix, the experiment created an empty control, an exact replay, a new-seed empty continuation and six insertions: arithmetic verification, correctness affirmation, error assertion, a hash sign, failure feedback and success feedback. The replay comparison required identical generated IDs and finish reason. Insertions retained their exact newline tokens.

Arithmetic and error assertion each occupied 15 tokens; failure and success feedback each occupied 14; affirmation occupied eight and the hash insertion two. Token length matching controls length within a prefix and branch seed, not token identity or meaning. The total generated-path cap was 32,768: inherited generated tokens reduced the remaining allowance, while inserted tokens were separately recorded.

A1 had 36 terminal job slots, of which 28 generated output. Q3 supplied a real baseline but no qualifying trigger, so its six treatments, replay and new-seed continuation were skipped. Its 25 scientific paths comprise four baselines, three new-seed controls and 18 treatments; three replays are additional engineering records. A1000 generated 32 scientific paths and four replays.

Repeated logical references to the same empty control are not extra observations. Physical output, counting each stem and branch once and including replays, was 34,011 and 130,113 tokens, respectively; repeated inherited prefixes are excluded from those costs.

Stage 3 joint-question preparation

The context preparation used ten conditions: each stage's task formulation with its baseline and four evaluation levels. Each condition generated two four-question streams simultaneously with batch size 2, yielding 20 streams and 80 dependent answer slots. A wrapper required ordered ACTION_Q lines and superseded local single-answer instructions. The question order was fixed.

Seeds varied by condition and replica; comparisons describe realized paths rather than isolate wording. The native output total was 261,559 tokens. Strict slot scoring retains whole-stream termination and output-contract requirements; content-level readings remain separate from the saved score.

Stage 4 registration and sampling

The sampling frame comprised 227 unique execution templates after normalizing the generatedpath cap to 32,768 and merging nine equivalent candidates among 236. There were 178 originalprompt starts and 49 prefix continuations, including 42 injected templates. Incorrect, formatinvalid and length-capped historical outputs remained eligible. Engineering tests, unfinished jobs and skipped dependents were excluded. Template identity includes exact input IDs, any frozen generated prefix, insertion, budget and oracle. Historical baseline names remain provenance labels after budget normalization.

Ninety-six templates were sampled uniformly without replacement from the sorted frame.

Three separately drawn 32-byte operating-system entropy values seeded separate Python random.Random MT19937 streams for template selection, model seed and temperature. Model seeds were uniform in [0,2^63), rejecting duplicates; temperatures were uniform over integer values 500-700 divided by 1,000. The realized assignments contain 96 distinct seeds and 78 temperatures spanning 0.501-0.699. Raw entropy, draws, rejections, RNG states and the audit log are retained. An independent algorithmic recomputation reproduced all assignments; source and audit interpreter versions are specified in the Supplementary Information. Every included execution used batch size 1, SDPA, fresh DynamicCache, one beam, sampling, top-p 0.95, top-k 0 and repetition penalty 1. Exact registered IDs were reused. A new per-call generator was seeded before prefill; the prefill-ready snapshot recorded its state, first-new-token logits and cache/position/layout metadata. It did not save full KV tensors or recover the historical prefix's original consumed random state. The first-new-token snapshot is not a record of subsequent logits. Prompt and insertion tokens occupy context but are outside the generated-path cap. The interrupted original S4-034 was excluded and its replacement routed explicitly; 96 assignments, not 97 attempts, define the scientific collection. Native and contextual readouts THINK_END is native ID 151649 and EOS ID 151643. Closure occurrence, first position, subsequent token count and final termination were extracted independently. A cap-ended path is right-censored for natural termination length. Single-question strict scoring requires EOS, the saved reporting rule and oracle action; joint scoring preserves its four-slot contract. The parser's terminal region begins after the last closure. CHECK success is an additional named field, not inferred from a general secondary-metric label. Source-native coordinates are retained; paper token ordinals are one-based inclusive, while character intervals use zero-based Unicode positions. Inherited, injected and newly generated material have separate coordinate domains. Mechanical probes include eligible 4-gram matches, scale-specific distinct-n-gram ratios and exact native repetition. A literal hit is an observed shared fragment, not proof of semantic uptake; absence of a hit is not evidence that an instruction was unprocessed. Detection windows and cycle criteria remain collection-specific. Descriptive rates retain record, answer-slot or eligiblewindow denominators. The 4×4 non-additive share is descriptive; the 9/15 degree-of-freedom noise benchmark is 60%. Reordered-series benchmarks describe rank behaviour, not a new significance test. There is one realized path per historical condition-item cell and one new assignment per sampled Stage 4 template, so no population-level causal temperature effect or per-template event probability is estimated. The 18-code ledger describes relations among conditions, referents, intermediate values and later operations. O denotes observed, N not found in the specified reading and U unresolved. Codes overlap; O to O+U is a coding-uncertainty interval. Decision-doubt-reopening requires recurring decision revision without maintained resolution. Finite checking, repeated equations, length alone or stable decisions with label reinterpretation do not suffice. A retained repair applies to its relevant relation and later use, not global correctness. Stage 4's current-posterior code requires binding to the actual supplied readings; the broader historical Stage 1-2 assignments and their sensitivity analysis are retained, not pooled as a common prevalence. Stages 1-2 received full model-assisted reading with 1,926 selected anchors. The 160 nonbaseline records used requested gpt-6.1-sol/ultra readers; exact coding-model settings for the 16 baselines were not recorded. Stage 4 received six requested gpt-6.1-sol/ultra reading batches and coordinating adjudication, producing 1,016 selected anchors. These readers did not inherit the private parent conversation; host project memory may have been available. Stage 3 received source-located contextual analysis without a claim of a newly applied exhaustive 18-code prevalence ledger. Quote, coordinate and source checks establish traceability. Independent human inter-coder agreement was not measured.

Quality control and computational access

The workflow separates invalid execution, comparison-set contamination, probe misclassification and genuine task-process failure. For example, the interrupted attempt is excluded from scientific denominators; inherited material is not counted as new semantic production; an unauthorized label that preserves a stated mapping is not automatically a decision reversal. Stage 5 recovery and sampling-state comparisons

The delivered clean28 run registered seven groups of four paths: from-start replay (G0), selfprefix 100 (G100), self-prefix 500 (G500), foreign-prefix 500 (GX500), and a seed-reset counterpart to each continuation group. The original four groups did not reuse four fully matched hosts; the 12 restoration/reset pairs did match host, donor, complete input IDs, temperature, sampling parameters and budget. GX500 used a donor with a different question configuration.

The Supplementary Information specifies all host/donor assignments and the two overlappinghost comparisons, which are post hoc descriptions.

Stage 3 contributes 25 scientific paths in the first-action preparation, 32 in the fixed-1,000-token preparation and 20 joint-question streams. Seven engineering replays are separate records. Stage 4 adds 96 sampled-template trajectories, including five streams with four answer slots each. Stage 5 adds 28 formal paths, including four historical from-start replay assignments, with 6,000 prefix-recovery tokens counted separately as engineering checks. The resulting 377 formal path or stream records do not constitute 377 independent task worlds. Eight within-stage baseline pairs regenerated identical native-token sequences over their full overlaps: 56,142 positions in Stage 1 and 36,874 in Stage 2, totalling 93,016. These are fromstart executions under the recorded settings. The comparison demonstrates reproducibility of the observed history, while identifying input, hardware, sampling and batch composition as coordinates of the preparation. It neither compares unchanged inputs across stages nor measures equality of hidden states.

The 18-code reading ledger localized 1,926 evidence anchors. Treating supplied readings as unknown or generalizing them away occurred in 68/72 Stage 1 and 77/104 Stage 2 records. Some failures occurred after the actual readings had already been used correctly: S2_abundance1000_Q2 calculated the current posterior before later declaring the readings uncertain. Conversely, S2_opportunities3_Q2 preserved a repaired sensor relation through the purchase comparison. The empirical object therefore includes successful maintenance and repair as well as loss. Local arithmetic success, relation maintenance and terminal correctness are separate measurements.

Stage 4

sampled 96 of 227 deduplicated historical templates without replacement. Each received one new seed and a temperature from the registered 0.500-0.700 grid; all executions used serial batch size 1. Incorrect, format-invalid and cap-ended historical cases remained eligible. Seventysix selected templates began from their original prompts; 20 continued frozen prefixes, 17 with an injection. The sample generated 1,157,417 new tokens, with 44,721 inherited and 209 externally inserted tokens recorded separately. Historical endpoints did not uniquely determine the new endpoint (Fig 4). Of 75 historical EOS cases, 61 again reached EOS and 14 reached the cap; of 21 historical capped cases, 16 reached EOS and five remained capped. Historical settings and caps varied, so these transitions describe response portability under the registered preparation rather than an isolated temperature or seed effect. The current 77 EOS and 19 capped paths separate into 58/18 among prompt starts and 19/1 among prefix continuations. All 20 continuations differed from their historical full token sequences, yet immediate-closure class was retained in 19/20. Pattern recurrence can therefore coexist with sequence divergence. The archive also contains an unplanned engineering replay. A file-lock interruption stopped the first attempt at S4-034 after 28,848 tokens. Restarting the same assignment reproduced every overlapping native token before reaching 32,768. The matched portion includes closure and 19,416 subsequent tokens. The interrupted attempt is retained as engineering evidence and excluded from the 96 scientific records. This case demonstrates reproducibility of the prolonged path under the same recorded assignment, alongside the endpoint changes found under new assignments.

Stage 5

compared seven preparations in 28 paths. Four from-start paths reproduced their historical hosts completely: all 29,224 native tokens and their EOS endings matched. Twelve host-specific recovery checks reproduced the first 500 historical tokens, yielding 6,000 engineering tokens. Their cut-time sampling-generator states were reconstructed during verified replay, rather than captured in place during the historical runs. All eight self-prefix paths supplied with 100 or 500 original tokens and the corresponding reconstructed sampling state diverged from their historical continuations after 1-71 shared new tokens. Native-prefix preservation and sampling-state restoration were therefore insufficient for full recovery in these tested fresh-prefill configurations. This result adds observed failures to the recovery map while retaining the earlier successful replay comparisons. The 12 restoration-versus-seed-reset pairs held the host, supplied prefix, complete model input, sampling parameters and remaining allowance fixed. Each pair had identical saved first-step logits across 152,064 BF16 values, but different sampling-generator states. All paired continuations differed, with the first mismatch at new-token positions 1-49. Resetting the original integer seed and restoring the consumed sampling state were empirically different preparations even when the initial model scores matched.

Stages 1 -

2 exposed closure without termination, opposing item paths beneath pooled consumption, and computation without maintained reference. Stage 3 made shared symbolic histories experimentally branchable. Stage 4 showed that recurring response patterns and changed outcomes can be distinguished under registered variation. Stage 5 makes the conditions of exact recovery an experimental target: successful from-start replay coexists with failed selfprefix reconstruction and sampling-dependent branching. None of these uses requires the specimen to reproduce a human participant one to one.

Stage 1 -

2 and Stage 4 records received the documented full reading, and Stage 5 received full directed reading for the X/Y event definitions. The selected anchors and codes do not exhaust every scientifically useful path. The research team cannot disclose a close interpretation of every event. Preserving the complete record leaves further paths available for reanalysis and new interventions. This is a productive property of the model organism, not a requirement that the first study finish its explanatory programme. The model-assisted ledger supplies explicit definitions and source coordinates; independent human inter-coder agreement was not measured. Observed-to-observed-plus-unresolved ranges describe recorded coding uncertainty, not confidence intervals. Mechanical quote verification establishes location, not semantic validity. Narrowing the historical decision-cycle definition changed 83/176 assignments, demonstrating the importance of the operational boundary. Identified task failures remain scientific material; an invalid execution record, a mismatched comparison set or an oversensitive probe affects a different claim. The Y1-to-C counterexample shows how calibration can reject a proposed reversal while retaining the real reporting-contract failure. The specimen, four task worlds and execution policies define the present scale. Stage 4 is a sample across templates with one new assignment per template, not a factorial estimate of seed and temperature effects. Stage 5 identifies a finite observed set of configurations supporting token-exact recovery, alongside configurations in which recovery failed. The necessary and sufficient conditions defining that set remain to be established through explicit matched evidence. Its members are complete preparations-input, prefix, numerical execution, sampling initialization, budget and comparison horizon-not token strings or seeds alone. Neither token equality nor difference establishes equality or difference of every hidden state. Equal first-step logits do not establish equal subsequent logits or historical cache contents. Minimum sufficient prefill and the broader boundary of recoverability remain open measurements. These specifications preserve the successful replays while replacing a universal restoration claim with an experimentally extensible recovery map.

bitsandbytes 0.50.2 on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 Laptop GPU with 16 GB VRAM. No targeted weight update or fine-tuning was applied during these experiments. Model revision, tokenizer, prompt IDs, runtime, hardware, batch composition, randomization and stopping rules jointly specify the preparation. Stages 1-2 used sampling, temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, top-k 0, one beam, repetition penalty 1 and KV caching. Batch size was 2: Q1-Q2 used seed 20261027; Q3-Q4 used seed 20261028. Records declare no previous conversation or reused context cache. Each stage independently generated four 16,384-cap and four 32,768-cap baseline records. Their native integer sequences were compared over the entire overlap. Other Stage 1-2 conditions used the 32,768 actual cap. A prompted budget or deadline did not change that cap, wall time or available retries. Stage 1 supplied 18 conditions: two baselines and four levels in each of budget, attempts, time and penalty families. Stage 2 supplied 26: two baselines and four levels in each of allowance, opportunity, time, pass criterion, CHECK and COST families. The Stage 1 compact clause describes sensor accuracy and a reading together; Stage 2 adds "Observed sensor readings:" and an explicit symmetric-error/conditional-independence statement. Its archived prompt remains one string, not line-separated sensor labels. Several features changed between stages, so their contrast is not a grammar-only control. Exact prompts and family tables are retained in the Supplementary Information.Task and oracleY and Z are independent fair binary variables; Z does not determine the Y decision. Aster and Birch are conditionally independent symmetric sensors with accuracies 0.8 and 0.6. Q1-Q4 supply readings (1,0), (0,1), (1,1) and (0,0). A correct Y choice earns one unit and an incorrect choice zero. The current actions are Y0, Y1 and BUY. BUY acquires another independent 0.8accuracy reading at cost 0.05, before a later Y choice. Current posteriors P(Y=1) are 8/11, 3/11, 6/7 and 1/7. For disagreeing readings, buying yields expected accuracy 4/5 and net reward 0.75, exceeding 8/11. For agreeing readings, the extra reading does not improve expected optimal accuracy beyond 6/7. Oracle actions are consequently BUY, BUY, Y1 and Y0.

their source field and native sequence. Failed task paths remain part of the research material. Analysis of preserved IDs, recomputation of saved semantic rates, renewed contextual reading and fresh GPU generation are different operations. The original Stage 1-2 deterministic 11-step CPU workflow took 15.09 seconds in one archived Windows run, without model weights or GPU, with an allowance of roughly 1 GB per workspace. Original Stage 1-2 generation accumulated 37.35 GPU hours excluding loading and counting each batch once. Those timings are not estimates for the expanded Stage 1-5 analysis. Exact regeneration is specified within its execution stack: GPU architecture, model, driver/CUDA versions, floating-point reductions and PTX compilation can affect later sampled tokens. The archived settings support matched repeats and diagnosis of portability, rather than a promise of cross-device bitwise identity. Stage 5 generated 333,950 new formal-path tokens plus 8,800 supplied-prefix tokens; its 6,000 recovery-check tokens are additional engineering work. Directed model-assisted reading covered all 28 new texts, using either literal full text or reversible exact-paragraph folding with ordered occurrence references. X requires at least two decision-doubt-reopening rounds on one referent; Y requires explicit identification of an incompatibility in task conditions, numbers or roles. Valid, mistaken and unclear Y assignments remain separate. Threshold counts at two, three and five X rounds are confirmed lower bounds, not an optimized threshold curve. The 377 verified quotations establish traceability, not independent semantic agreement. The directed X/Y analysis does not constitute a new full 18-code prevalence ledger. Use of language models in research and manuscript preparation Language-model assistance was integral to experimental implementation, code development, source extraction, contextual reading, analytical interpretation, adversarial discussion, drafting and revision. The author-directed collaboration involved GPT systems through ChatGPT/Codex, DeepSeek, Gemini, GLM, Claude, Qwen and Kimi; the experimental specimen was DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B. Exact reader configurations are reported where recorded, rather than assigning an unrecorded version to a model family. Human authors determine the research questions, adopt or reject interpretations and retain responsibility for the manuscript. Automated records preserve execution and analysis provenance. Private author-model thought experiments are not part of the public data deposit. CMO_FullCorpus_Analysis_Supplement_20261030_r2.zip is retained unchanged. Full generation records and selected interpretive annotations remain distinct. The preprint version of this manuscript is identified at https://osf.io/preprints/psyarxiv/z4dhg_v3. The Supplementary Information provides preparation details, record units and analysis definitions. The project DOI is https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23748346.

All paths used serial batch size 1 and fresh DynamicCache prefill. The 32,768-token generatedpath cap included supplied prefixes and excluded the user prompt: 100-and 500-token prefixes left 32,668 and 32,268 new-token allowances. Temperature and seed were inherited from each host. G0 used the saved initial sampling-generator state. For later cuts, exact 500-token replay reconstructed the host generator's post-draw states at 100 and 500. Restoration loaded these bytes; seed reset initialized the original integer seed without advancing the omitted prefix draws. Historical KV tensor contents were not restored. The saved recovery logits at cut k predicted the just-sampled token k, whereas fresh-prefill logits predicted token k+1; only the position-matched scientific pairs were used for the reported logits-equality comparison. Token-exact recovery was evaluated against a named reference and horizon. Supplied prefix tokens were excluded from continuation recovery scores. Full recovery required identical newly generated native IDs, equal continuation length and equal finish reason. Overlap agreement under unequal caps established identity only over the compared positions. A capped match would not establish natural termination. Tested preparations were classified as observed successes or failures under this criterion; untested preparations remained unclassified. This finite classification does not yet specify necessary and sufficient recovery conditions. Shared final labels, preserved task relations and complete internal-state equality are different claims.
